quizName: Hardest Questions in Tennessee Most difficult questions from your region.

questions.question: What should be your first priority when buying a motorcycle helmet?
questions.explanation: Protection should be your first priority. Choose a helmet that fastens securely, fits correctly, and has a DOT label.

questions.question: At night, judging distances is:

options.text: About the same as during the day.

questions.explanation: It is harder to judge distances at night than during the day. Shadows and light help you see distance. At night, artificial lights may distort these clues or remove them completely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They tell drivers about traffic laws in that area. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will enter the roadway ahead.
Come to a complete stop, then go when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop, then go when safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. You must come to a complete stop, let other traffic and pedestrians pass, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: Taking over-the-counter medicine before riding:

options.text: Is usually fine because over-the-counter medicines are weak.
May harm your riding and should be done carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: May harm your riding and should be done carefully.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including over-the-counter medicines, can make it unsafe to ride. Talk to your doctor about how new medicine might affect your riding.

questions.question: If you borrow a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Assume the controls are in the same spots as your bike.
Take it right out on the highway.
Learn how it works in a safe area first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Learn how it works in a safe area first.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Before riding an unfamiliar bike, find all the controls. Practice in a safe area before riding on the road.

questions.question: You have a better chance of surviving a crash if you wear:
questions.explanation: A helmet that meets DOT standards gives you the best head and neck protection. Wearing a good helmet that is fastened securely is the best thing you can do to survive a crash.

questions.question: Which material gives the best protection for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather and strong synthetic materials give riders the most protection.

questions.question: Before every ride, you should:

options.text: Test that your brake lights work.
Check that the paint is not peeling.
Make sure the bike is completely clean.

questions.correctAnswerText: Test that your brake lights work.
questions.explanation: Do safety checks before every ride. Test both brake controls to make sure each one turns on the brake lights.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that a railroad crossing is coming.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what should riders do?

options.text: All keep a safe distance from each other.
Follow each other as closely as possible.
Not worry about distances between members.

questions.correctAnswerText: All keep a safe distance from each other.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, use a staggered formation. This keeps riders close together while maintaining safe distances between them.

questions.question: What lane position should you pick?

options.text: One that makes you visible and gives you safe space around your bike.
Any position you like, without thinking about others.
One that gets you close to other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: One that makes you visible and gives you safe space around your bike.
questions.explanation: Pick a lane position where other drivers can see you best. Make sure you have a space cushion around your motorcycle. Change your position as road conditions change.

questions.question: What is a benefit of reflective and brightly-colored helmets and clothing?

options.text: They should only be worn when riding at night.
They help other drivers see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: They help other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: Bright colors and reflective gear increase your chances of being seen by other drivers.

questions.question: What kind of boots or shoes should you wear when riding?

options.text: Ones with long and loose laces.

questions.explanation: Wear sturdy footwear that covers and supports your ankles. Heels should be low so they don't catch on surfaces. Tuck in shoelaces so they don't get caught on the motorcycle.

questions.question: Where should a passenger sit on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Passengers must sit behind the operator and hold onto the operator's waist or midsection. They can also hold onto handgrips if the motorcycle has them. Passengers should never ride sidesaddle.

questions.question: What should you do when nearing a blind intersection?

options.text: Assume that other drivers will yield the right-of-way.
Change your lane position to be more visible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your lane position to be more visible.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, move to the lane position where other drivers can see you best.

questions.question: What should you do if you must ride on a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, reduce your speed. Avoid sudden moves. Use both brakes carefully.

questions.question: How should your helmet fit to give you the most protection?
questions.explanation: Your helmet protects you best when it meets DOT standards, fits snugly all the way around, and has no damage.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, what should you wear?

options.text: Only wear a jacket at night.
Only wear a jacket if it is cold.

questions.explanation: Always wear a sturdy jacket with long sleeves when riding, even in warm weather.

questions.question: What should you look for when choosing a helmet?

options.text: It has no cracks or defects.

questions.correctAnswerText: It has no cracks or defects.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets DOT standards. It should fit snugly all the way around. Check for damage like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: Motorcycles have blind spots. What should riders do about them?

options.text: Check them regularly by turning your head.
They do not exist if you have a rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check them regularly by turning your head.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like all vehicles. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes. Make head checks part of your normal riding routine.

questions.question: When buying a motorcycle helmet, what should matter most?
questions.explanation: Protection is your most important concern when choosing a motorcycle helmet.

questions.question: What is the effect of improper braking on motorcycles?

options.text: It is not a concern because motorcycles have two brakes.

questions.explanation: Improper braking causes many motorcycle crashes. Using correct braking technique is essential for safe riding.

questions.question: How can you make yourself more visible to other drivers?
questions.explanation: Wearing bright clothing helps other drivers see you. This is important at any time of day.

questions.question: How can you reduce fatigue on long rides?
questions.explanation: Frequent rest breaks help reduce fatigue during long trips. Caffeine may make fatigue worse when it wears off. Weather conditions like wind and rain increase fatigue, so dress warmly and use a windshield on long rides.

questions.question: What is the most important feature of motorcycle riding clothing?

options.text: It protects you in a crash.
It should not stand out to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: It protects you in a crash.
questions.explanation: Good riding clothes protect you in a crash while keeping you comfortable and visible to other drivers.

questions.question: Why should you use your mirrors when stopping at an intersection?

options.text: To check if drivers behind you see you stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: To check if drivers behind you see you stopping.
questions.explanation: Always check your mirrors at intersections to make sure drivers behind you see that you are stopping. This helps you know if they are paying attention to you.

questions.question: What color clothing should you wear when riding?
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors to make yourself visible, even during the day. Reflective materials also help other drivers see you.

questions.question: When stopping with a passenger, what should you do differently?

options.text: Start slowing down earlier than normal.
Merge into smaller traffic gaps than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Start slowing down earlier than normal.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle, making it slower to respond. It takes longer to speed up, slow down, and turn. Start slowing earlier, reduce your speed, and look for larger traffic gaps when carrying a passenger.

questions.question: What happens when you drink alcohol quickly?

options.text: It builds up in your body faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: It builds up in your body faster.
questions.explanation: The faster you drink, the faster alcohol builds up in your body. Your body removes alcohol at about one drink per hour. If you drink more than one drink per hour, alcohol stays in your system.
